system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Wattlebridge Holdings | Project Kestrel**

The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and “agreed” labels are not evidence of Buyer approval or market practice. Review all positions against the **AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition**. The recommendations below are Buyer negotiating positions, subject to the complete SPA and underlying DD documents, which have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery proportionate to exposure, with separate treatment of fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to DD and available recourse; negotiate any reduction alongside the entire protection package. **Reason:** A 20% cap leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer and is not justified merely by a “standard” label. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds; related claims aggregated; a tipping basket, recovering all qualifying losses once crossed; no thresholds for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, aggregating connected claims. **Reason:** The proposed combination permanently excludes meaningful losses and could fragment related claims below threshold. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General claims notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, with longer category-specific periods; timely notified claims survive until resolved. | **Seek 36 months, with 24 months as a negotiated fallback**, and reject universal application. **Reason:** Eighteen months may not capture latent problems or a sufficient post-acquisition reporting cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate protection for authority, capacity, ownership, share capital and unencumbered transfer; no de minimis or basket. | **Require a separate 100%-of-price cap and six-year notification period**, without erosion by general claims. **Reason:** Buyer should not bear the risk that Seller cannot validly transfer the business it is selling. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud and fraudulent-misrepresentation claims, including appropriate attribution for persons acting for Seller; preservation of non-excludable rights. | **Carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, knowledge/disclosure defences and remedy/reliance restrictions.** **Reason:** Seller must not use the contractual protection package to shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, mapped to relevant warranties; a fixed, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure; require specific, fair disclosure and a frozen indexed archive.** **Reason:** Mere availability of information should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer or neutralise warranties wholesale. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from data-room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal principals, without imputation, constructive knowledge or duty to investigate. | **Delete the qualifier; accept only a tightly defined actual-knowledge fallback if commercially necessary.** **Reason:** “Discoverable” information and adviser knowledge could defeat claims despite inadequate Seller disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions. | Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring valid consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without materially adverse amendments, charges or termination rights. | **Require the complete consent package and evidence of effectiveness before Completion, with a longstop/termination right.** **Reason:** Bluefen represents approximately 30% of revenue, and a conditional consent letter alone may not protect that revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release supplied after Completion. | Debt repaid through Completion funds flow, reducing Seller proceeds without double counting; binding payoff and release mechanics effective at Completion. | **Require a lender payoff letter, direct repayment, discharge of all relevant security and release of guarantees at Completion**, with registration follow-up controlled. **Reason:** Debt-free/cash-free delivery is not achieved while acquisition-triggered debt or lender security remains outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; associated on-costs unspecified. | Seller economically bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation, withholding and other on-costs, without double counting. | **Quantify and include the liability in funds flow/price adjustments, backed by a specific indemnity for residual exposure.** **Reason:** Calling bonuses a Seller matter does not prevent the acquired company—and therefore Buyer—from having to pay them. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity confined to the specific SOW3 payment; transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 recorded open, without independent payment verification. | Verified payment and an effective assignment/release covering all relevant materials and rights; protection against ownership, infringement and remediation exposure arising from this matter. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment before Completion, plus a broader specific indemnity outside general warranty limits.** **Reason:** Paying the recorded balance alone may neither establish IP ownership nor cover downstream losses. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter said not to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, containment, evidence preservation, legal assessment of notification duties and appropriate remediation; protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require a documented investigation and response plan, a specific indemnity and consideration of retention or a completion condition if findings warrant.** **Reason:** Uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but the current record also does not establish a confirmed breach or loss. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and consistency with ordinary course; control new commitments before Completion. | **Review the renewals together and require Buyer approval where outside agreed ordinary-course limits; adjust price only where the agreed mechanics justify it.** **Reason:** Related commitments can be material collectively, but future operating expenditure is not automatically debt-like. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply across all Claims unless expressly excepted. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, payment/adjustment obligations and fraud; clear priority rules. | **Redraft the definitions and operative provisions so each category expressly has its own cap, thresholds, duration and exceptions.** **Reason:** An “all Claims” override could silently strip negotiated protections from otherwise separate obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Company share register identifies Harbourglass as holder of 100%; Seller treats it as evidence of title. | Independent verification of legal and beneficial ownership, issued capital, encumbrances, options and competing rights, supported by effective transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records and capital history; obtain appropriate searches, certificates/declarations, releases and executed transfers.** **Reason:** The register is important evidence, not conclusive verification of the entire ownership and encumbrance position. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled under the general limitation regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity and suitable tax warranties; robust IP ownership, assignment, licensing, infringement and open-source protections. | **Reopen both:** seek tax protection through relevant assessment/reassessment periods plus a notification buffer, and a separately negotiated IP cap/duration, preserving the Ironquay indemnity. **Reason:** Tax and core SaaS IP risks can emerge after 18 months and materially exceed the general recovery package. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, Ironquay ownership evidence, and a corrected funds flow including bonuses and applicable on-costs. The lease and Mossvale disclosures should not, without supporting contractual wording, be converted into share-sale consent requirements.
=== END ADVICE ===
